charts.name: Malawi reference chart of accounts
charts.legal_reference: There is no legal chart of accounts in Malawi. The Institute of Chartered Accountants in Malawi (ICAM), which holds the authority to adopt accounting standards under the Public Accountants and Auditors Act 2012, adopted IFRS in 2001 and IFRS for SMEs for entities that are not publicly accountable. This chart is original: four digits, blocked so that each range reaches one line of the IFRS-based statements below, with the accounts a Malawian company actually keeps — VAT input and output tax, import VAT owed to the Malawi Revenue Authority at the border, withholding tax, PAYE, pension contributions and excise duty payable.

numbering.legal_reference: Value Added Tax Act, s. 25(1) and (2) — a taxable person issues an electronic fiscal device generated tax invoice, or a tax invoice in the prescribed form, and keeps a copy in serial number order; s. 30(1)(b) — input tax on a local purchase is deductible only against a tax invoice issued under s. 25. Malawian law asks for a serial number and not for a series with no gap, which is why `numbering` is `sequential`.

tax_point.legal_reference: Value Added Tax Act, s. 24 — the time of supply. The section was read in the 2014 consolidation only; it names a time of supply by delivery, invoice and payment, and Ekwo's closed vocabulary expresses `earliest_of_delivery_or_payment`, the nearest value. The wording of the section has to be confirmed against the current Act.

einvoicing.legal_reference: No Malawian text this pack could open obliges a business to exchange a structured electronic invoice with another business in the sense Ekwo's vocabulary gives the word: there is no Peppol authority, no published profile and no scheme a party is addressed by, so `profile`, `party_scheme` and `vat_scheme` are null and `obligation` is `none`. What Malawi has is a clearance system run by the Malawi Revenue Authority: s. 25 of the Value Added Tax Act (2014 consolidation) requires an electronic fiscal device generated tax invoice or a prescribed tax invoice, and the Authority runs an Electronic Invoicing System (EIS) with a point-of-sale management portal that replaces electronic fiscal devices. The Authority's own notices on the EIS (start date, who must use it, penalties) could not be opened; trade commentary reports a transition ending on 31 January 2026 and mandatory use from 1 May 2026, which this pack does not rely on. That is real-time clearance with the tax administration and not a peer-to-peer exchange; the gap is recorded in docs/international.md and in this pack's README, and the socle is not patched to fit it.
